forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MPH5DRJ6BEFCX0VBTZVB81
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: 8d80
+title: 'Doctor checks 4 to 7: initialize answers in time, the version and capabilities read, and nothing leaks'
+---
+## What
+
+`cli-plan.md` §10, the last four rows of the check table. They all run over one
+live connection to the agent, so they extend the `AgentCommandDoctor` that the
+previous task created in `Sources/acp-client/AgentCommandDoctor.swift`.
+
+4. **`initialize` answers inside a time limit.** Connect over the
+   `AgentProcess` transport, send `initialize`, and race it against the
+   doctor's time limit. A limit that ends first is an `error` that reports a
+   timeout, and never a hang: the check must return, and the suite must not
+   wait.
+5. **The protocol version is one we support.**
+   `ClientSideConnection.initialize(_:)` already validates that the agent
+   answered with the version that was sent, and throws
+   `ProtocolVersionMismatchError` naming both versions. Catch that error and
+   turn it into an `error` check whose message holds both versions, so the
+   report says "a v1 agent, or a newer draft" in concrete terms.
+6. **The advertised capabilities are readable.** A malformed `initialize`
+   result gives a decoding failure. Report it as an `error` naming the field
+   that failed.
+7. **The process ends when its stdin closes, and it leaves no child.** Close
+   the agent's stdin, wait a bounded interval, and check the pid is gone with
+   `kill(pid, 0)`. An agent that is still running is a `warning`, not an
+   `error`: it is usable, and it leaks. The `fix` text says a leaked agent
+   holds gigabytes of model weights.
+
+Row 7 is the one row that gives a `warning`, and it is why `cli-plan.md` §9
+needs exit code 5 at all.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] `silentAgent` gives an `error` on row 4 whose message says the limit was
+      reached, and `runHealthChecks()` returns inside that limit.
+- [ ] An agent that answers `initialize` with a version other than the one
+      sent gives an `error` on row 5 naming both versions.
+- [ ] An agent that answers `initialize` with a malformed result gives an
+      `error` on row 6.
+- [ ] `wellBehavedAgent` gives `ok` on rows 4 to 7.
+- [ ] An agent that ignores a closed stdin gives a `warning` on row 7, and the
+      whole report's `worstStatus` is `warning`.
+- [ ] Rows 4 to 7 are skipped when row 1 or row 2 already failed.
+- [ ] No agent process outlives `runHealthChecks()`, in every branch above.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] Extend
+      `IntegrationTests/Tests/FoundationModelsACPClientIntegrationTests/AgentCommandDoctorTests.swift`,
+      one test per acceptance row above.
+- [ ] Extend `StubAgents` with three more scripts: one that answers
+      `initialize` with a wrong protocol version, one that answers with a
+      malformed result object, and one that ignores a closed stdin and keeps
+      running.
+- [ ] One test bounds the whole `silentAgent` case with a deadline and fails
+      when `runHealthChecks()` does not return inside it.
+- [ ] One test asserts the pid of each stub is gone after the run, with
+      `kill(pid, 0)`.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --package-path IntegrationTests`. Every assertion
+      passes.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
